therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: antimicrobial activity reducing oral bacterial load
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: prevention of bacterial translocation from oral cavity to respiratory tract
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: patients undergoing lung cancer or esophageal cancer resection
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: number of participants who develop postoperative pneumonia within 30 days of surgery

results.effect_size: 6 total pneumonia cases (5 esophageal, 1 lung resection patients)
subgroup_findings: Higher pneumonia rate in esophageal resection patients (5/43) vs lung resection patients (1/62)
safety_signals: Perioperative mortality: 0 esophageal, 3 lung resection patients
Respiratory failure: 5 esophageal, 5 lung resection patients
results.dose_information: toothbrushing 3 times/day for at least 5 days preoperatively and for duration of hospitalization or 5 days postoperatively

context.duration: 5 days preoperative + hospitalization/5 days postoperative, 30-day follow-up
context.investigator_commentary: Slow patient accrual and plans to perform multi-center study
